unpinned_install_fix_round.note: The original commands used `uv pip install crawl4ai` / `uv pip install browser-use` with no version constraint, then read the installed version back afterward -- the review is right that this is not what 'install ... at pinned versions' means. FIX ROUND: re-ran `uv pip install "crawl4ai==0.9.3"` and `uv pip install "browser-use==0.13.10"` in the same venvs; both resolved to the already-installed pin with no changes (`Checked 1 package in ...ms`), confirming 0.9.3 / 0.13.10 are exact, reproducible pins rather than whatever-latest-resolved-that-day.

cua_driver_probe_fix_round.install: uv venv + `uv pip install cua-computer` succeeded cleanly (cua-computer 0.5.19, cua-core 0.3.1, no paid dependency pulled in).
cua_driver_probe_fix_round.why_not_run_further: Computer.__init__ requires either a running local 'Computer Server' via use_host_computer_server, or a VM provider (default: Lume, macOS-only; Docker-backed Linux/Windows VM images are multi-GB and not preinstalled) -- there is no lightweight in-process CDP-style driver comparable to agent-browser's or browser-use's. Exercising it would mean either standing up a new VM/container image (a heavy job, and this host has no macOS/Lume) or supplying a Cua Cloud api_key (excluded: 'no paid API, no credential reads'). This is a genuine infrastructure gap, not a time-box skip: Cua Driver remains installed-but-functionally-untested after this round.
cua_driver_probe_fix_round.verdict: advanced from 'source review only' to 'package installs cleanly; execution requires infrastructure (VM/container or cloud key) outside this unit's isolation and no-paid-API bounds' -- still not functionally tested.

outcome_detail: FIX ROUND (independent review): downgraded from 'settled' -- the gap names four tools and the original pass only exercised two, so 'settled' overstated closure. Corrected picture: Crawl4AI 0.9.3 fetched and correctly extracted markdown from the loopback fixture, but its own heuristic anti-bot detector flagged the tiny fixture page as 'Blocked by anti-bot protection: Structural: minimal_text' and marked the result success=False despite a correct fetch/scrape -- a real false-positive on small pages. It passed cleanly on example.com. Browser Use 0.13.10 (CDP-based navigation, no LLM/agent loop, no paid API): this round exercised fill+click, not just navigation -- TypeTextEvent + ClickElementEvent on the fixture's #name/#greet, verified via a CDP Runtime.evaluate readback of #status ('Hello, Gap Wave 2 Fix!'), the same round trip agent-browser's fixture uses. Separately, `get_current_page_title()` still returns the bare hostname/URL rather than the page's actual <title> on both pages -- a real accessor quirk at this version. Both installs are now confirmed pinned (0.9.3 / 0.13.10) via an explicit `pkg==version` re-install rather than only reading the version back after an unconstrained install. Cua Driver and Firecrawl MCP were probed, not just left as source-review: Cua Driver's Python package installs cleanly but requires either a macOS/Lume VM, a Docker VM image, or a paid Cua Cloud API key to actually drive anything -- none available/in-scope here, so it remains functionally untested for an infrastructure reason, not a time-box one. Firecrawl MCP's CLI confirms a genuine free/keyless mode exists for `firecrawl_scrape`/`firecrawl_search`, but a live MCP protocol call attempted this round did not complete within 60s and is recorded as not_settled, not tested. Net: 2 of 4 named tools (Crawl4AI, Browser Use) now have fuller functional coverage including the fill/click round trip; the other 2 (Cua Driver, Firecrawl MCP) are advanced from pure source-review to a concrete, recorded reason each remains untested.
limits: Cua Driver was probed for installability only; no VM/container was started and no functional browser-control call was made (infrastructure and no-paid-API constraints, not a skip).

Firecrawl MCP was probed for install/--help only; a live keyless tools/call was attempted and timed out at 60s without a response -- the stdio JSON-RPC client script used for that attempt is not retained in this repo (host-local only), so the exact hang point is not independently reproducible from these artifacts; treat the firecrawl_scrape/firecrawl_search keyless capability as plausible-per-its-own---help-text but not confirmed working end to end.

Browser Use was exercised only via its low-level CDP navigation/event API (navigate, fill, click, one JS readback), never its LLM-driven agent loop (which would need a paid model API call and is out of scope); agentic task-completion behavior is still unqualified.

crawl4ai-setup wrote its Playwright browser download to the default ~/.cache/ms-playwright and its local database to ~/.crawl4ai/ rather than the isolated ~/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/web-research prefix during the original run. FIX ROUND: both directories were removed after confirming (via `stat`) they were created during this unit's run window and not present before it -- isolation is now clean going forward, but this documents that the breach happened and was corrected, not that it never occurred.

Reproducibility: scripts/crawl4ai_test.py, scripts/browseruse_test.py and scripts/browseruse_fillclick_test.py are committed; raw/crawl4ai_results.json, raw/browseruse_results.json and raw/browseruse_fillclick_results.json are the retained raw outputs. The Cua Driver and Firecrawl MCP probe commands (uv pip install / npx --help / the ad hoc MCP client) were run interactively and are described in cua_driver_probe_fix_round / firecrawl_mcp_probe_fix_round above rather than saved as scripts.
